name: Ohio-class submarine
headline: length
subtitle: US Navy ballistic missile submarine (SSBN)
description: The Ohio class is the US Navy's fleet of nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarines, often called 'boomers', built by General Dynamics Electric Boat. The Navy lists each boat at 560 ft (170.69 m) long with a 42 ft beam, displacing 18,750 tons when submerged. The Navy lists 14 boats, each now carrying up to 20 Trident II D5 missiles, and the Columbia class is planned to replace them.

facts.text: There are 14 Ohio-class ballistic missile submarines, based at Bangor, Washington, and Kings Bay, Georgia.
Each boat originally carried up to 24 missiles; under the New START treaty four tubes on each were permanently deactivated, leaving a maximum of 20.
Each submarine has two crews, Blue and Gold, that take turns on patrol. On average a boat spends 77 days at sea, then 35 days in port for maintenance.
The crew is 15 officers and 144 enlisted sailors, and the top speed is given as 20+ knots.
The replacement Columbia class is also 560 ft long, with a 43 ft beam and a displacement of 20,800 long tons.

sources.title: Fleet Ballistic Missile Submarines - SSBN (fact file, last updated 27 Feb 2025)

caveats: navy.mil returns HTTP 403 to plain fetches, so the fact file was read in headless Chrome.
Displacement is the mass of water pushed aside by the hull, which equals the submarine's mass when floating. The Navy's 'tons' are long tons; the metric figures are stored.
The four Ohio-class boats converted to guided-missile submarines (SSGN) are not covered by this fact file.
No height (hull depth or sail height) was found in the Navy source, so only the length axis is drawn.
